As for the verbal Sunnah, there is what is established in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ): that Allah said: "I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves. When he says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah says: 'My servant has praised Me.' When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, He says: 'My servant has extolled Me.' When he says: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾, He says: 'My servant has glorified Me.' When he says: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾, He says: 'This is between Me and My servant in halves, and for My servant is what he asks.' When he says: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked anger or of those who are astray﴾, He says: 'This is for My servant, and for My servant is what he asks.'"[[Recorded by Muslim (395/38) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]

The first: at-Tur, which is the mountain upon which Allah spoke to Musa ibn 'Imran (peace be upon him). Allah first spoke to him on the mountain of at-Tur, so this mountain had a nobility and virtue that set it apart from other mountains. For this reason many scholars have stated that it (i.e., the mountain of at-Tur) is the best and most noble of mountains.

According to this, it would be more noble and more virtuous than Mount Hira', where revelation first began for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is the apparent implication of the statement of many scholars.

However, this generalization requires scrutiny, because the Messenger (ﷺ) was addressed at Hira', but it was Jibril who was sent with the message from Allah. Thus from it began the best of messages to the best of messengers.

Also: Hira' is within the Sacred Precinct of Makkah, for it is part of the sanctuary whose game may not be hunted and whose trees may not be cut, and the sacred precinct is the best of places. The statement of many scholars may be understood in this sense, so it is said: except Mount Hira'.

According to this, the intended meaning of "the inscribed Book" must be the Noble Qur'an.

His saying ﴿unrolled﴾ is an adjective of ﴿Book﴾, and it may be an adjective of ﴿parchment﴾, and the meaning is the same.

By "unrolled" is meant spread out, which is in the hands of every reader, and this applies perfectly to the Noble Qur'an, for it is—praise be to Allah—in the hands of every reader, even the young among the Muslims read it.

Now let us consider whether there is any contradiction between the sworn-by thing being the Ka'bah or the much-frequented House in the heavens. Then look again, twice﴾ [al-Mulk 3, 4]; i.e., time after time. ﴿Your sight will return to you humbled, and it will be fatigued﴾ [al-Mulk 4]. If we looked at this sea according to what nature dictates, we would say: it must overflow onto the earth and drown it. There are things for which we see no counterpart on land, and these are signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾ [at-Tur 7]. This is the answer to the oath, and the sentence here is emphasized by three emphases, indeed by three: the multiple oath, five oaths; the lam in His saying ﴿surely going to occur﴾, and ﴿indeed﴾ in His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord﴾. This sentence is emphasized by three emphatic elements: by an oath on five things, and when it is an oath by five things it is as if He swore by them five times. The second: by ﴿inna﴾. The third: by the lam.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾ [at-Tur 7]; i.e., the punishment of Allah that He promised must occur. By Allah, this is a great and impactful sentence, but it affects only a heart that is soft, as soft as butter or even more so. As for a hard heart, it pays it no heed; it passes over it as if it were ice. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he recited this verse, would fall ill until he was visited, he would become ill from the intensity of the impact upon his heart until he was visited. If it is certain to occur and there is no repeller for it, is it not fitting for us to fear? Indeed, by Allah, this is the fitting response.

His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾; i.e., it must occur. But is this emphasis regarding the punishment of believers or the punishment of disbelievers? Let us consider. Allah says: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely occur, for the disbelievers, which none can repel, from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ [al-Ma'arij 1–3]. Join this verse to the verse in at-Tur and you will find that His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur, there is none to repel it﴾ [at-Tur 7, 8] is upon whom? Upon the disbelievers. So Allah's punishment upon the disbelievers has no repeller; no one repels it, neither before it occurs nor after it occurs, and for this reason intercession will not benefit them, and the punishment is not lifted from them.

As for Allah's punishment upon the believer, the principle is that it is going to occur; every sin for which Allah threatened punishment, the principle is that it will occur, but nevertheless it may be lifted by a grace from Allah, Mighty and Majestic: it may be lifted by intercession, it may be lifted by righteous deeds that overwhelm the evil deeds. Have you not seen that Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa' 48]? Do you not know that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim dies and forty men stand over his funeral prayer who do not associate anything with Allah, except that Allah accepts their intercession for him"[[Recorded by Muslim (948/59) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], so the punishment is lifted from him.

Accordingly we say: the punishment of Allah upon the disbelievers will certainly occur, and there is no repeller for it; as for the sinful believers, the principle is that it occurs, for what prevents it when Allah has warned His servants, made them fear, and clarified for them? Nevertheless it may be lifted by various causes.

﴿there is none to repel it﴾ [at-Tur 8]: "ma" is negating, and "dafi'" (repeller) is a postponed subject, with the superfluous "min" entering upon it for emphasis; i.e., no one, however great his station and strength, can repel the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, never. He neither prevents it nor lifts it; for "dafi'" here, O brothers, includes both prevention and lifting: it includes prevention before occurrence and lifting after occurrence. No one repels the punishment of Allah; it cannot be prevented from descending nor lifted once it has descended, and that belongs to Allah alone.

What appears is that there is no contradiction, for both houses are venerated: that one is venerated among the people of the heavens, and this one is venerated among the people of the earth, and there is no obstacle.

So the correct view is that the verse includes both this and that, unless there is an indication that favors the much-frequented House in the heavens.

﴿and by the raised canopy﴾: Allah swore by the raised canopy, which is the sky. Allah says: ﴿Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars you can see﴾ [ar-Ra'd 2], and He says: ﴿And We made the sky a protected canopy﴾ [al-Anbiya' 32]. So the sky is a canopy, and the sky is raised.

Therefore the raised canopy is the sky, and Allah called it a canopy because it covers the whole earth from all sides, as a ceiling covers a room from all sides. Allah swore by the sky because of the great signs in it: stars, sun, moon, firmness and perfection. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So look again: do you see any flaw? Then look again, twice﴾ [al-Mulk 3, 4]; i.e., time after time. ﴿Your sight will return to you humbled, and it will be fatigued﴾ [al-Mulk 4]. He informed that there are no rifts in the sky, no cracks, no defect, no fissures, and it does not decay over a long period; it is worthy that Allah swear by it.

﴿and by the swollen sea﴾: the word "sea" has been said to refer to the sea upon which is the Throne of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, as He says: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾ [Hud 7]. It has also been said that it refers to the sea on earth, because it is observed, a known thing in which are signs of Allah that dazzle the minds.

The correct view is that it refers to the sea of the earth, because the "al" in ﴿the sea﴾ is the mental definite article (al-'ahd adh-dhihni), i.e., the known sea that you recognize. Allah swore by it because of the great signs of Allah in it: fish, waves, and other things that we know and that we do not know.

Among the greatest signs of Allah in it is what He alluded to in His saying ﴿al-masjur﴾; i.e., restrained, and from it comes the expression "sajar the dog," meaning in the lexicon: he tied it so it would not flee. The meaning here is not... in the lexicon it is said: sajarat al-kalb, i.e., I tied the dog so that it would not escape. ﴿the swollen sea﴾ restrained by whose power? By the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

We all know that the earth is spherical, and if we looked at this sea according to the nature of things, it would overflow onto the earth, because there are no walls to prevent it, and the earth is round like a ball. If we looked at this sea according to what nature dictates, we would say: it must overflow onto the earth and drown it. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, holds it back by His power, Glorified and Exalted is He, so it is restrained, i.e., prevented from overflowing onto the earth and drowning its people, and this is one of the signs of Allah.

Pour water on top of one of the balls; where does it go? It covers it to the right and to the left. But this sea cannot overflow onto the earth by the power of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He. Consider the wisdom: at times come the days of the tide and ebb, and the same sea extends enormously by many meters and perhaps miles, then it recedes. Who extended it, and if He willed it would have remained extended and the earth would drown? And who returned it? It is Allah, and for this reason this sea is worthy that Allah swear by it.

In the sea are great signs. It is said that there is nothing on land of animals and trees except that it has a counterpart in the sea, and more; for the sea, in relation to dry land, represents roughly seventy percent, which is very large. There are in it things that are not on land: a fish in the shape of a human, in the shape of a wolf, in the shape of a hyena, in the shape of a snake, in the shape of a scorpion. There are things for which we see no counterpart on land, and these are signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿and the swollen sea﴾: so the greatest sign in the sea is that it is restrained, i.e., prevented from overflowing onto the earth and drowning its people.

It has also been said that the intended meaning of ﴿al-masjur﴾ is that which will be set alight (sujjirat), i.e., kindled, as Allah says: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [at-Takwir 6]; i.e., kindled. So these are two views.

Regarding ﴿the swollen sea﴾: the first view is the restrained, and ﴿the swollen sea﴾ which will be set alight, i.e., kindled, and when will that be? On the Day of Resurrection. This water that we observe now, into which if a live coal fell or passed over a coal it would extinguish it, will on the Day of Resurrection become fire; this water will be set alight and become fire. This is one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

These are two views: the first view: the restrained, prevented from overflowing onto the earth and drowning its people. The second: the one that will be set alight, i.e., kindled, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection.

Can we say that both meanings are intended? Yes, for there is no contradiction between them, and both are signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; i.e., whether we say al-masjur is the restrained from overflowing onto the earth, or al-masjur is what will be set alight, i.e., kindled, all of that is among the signs of Allah.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾ [at-Tur 7]. This is the answer to the oath, and the sentence here is emphasized by three emphases, indeed by three: the multiple oath, five oaths; the lam in His saying ﴿surely going to occur﴾, and ﴿indeed﴾ in His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord﴾. This sentence is emphasized by three emphatic elements: by an oath on five things, and when it is an oath by five things it is as if He swore by them five times. The second: by ﴿inna﴾. The third: by the lam.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾ [at-Tur 7]; i.e., the punishment of Allah that He promised must occur. By Allah, this is a great and impactful sentence, but it affects only a heart that is soft, as soft as butter or even more so. As for a hard heart, it pays it no heed; it passes over it as if it were ice. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he recited this verse, would fall ill until he was visited, he would become ill from the intensity of the impact upon his heart until he was visited. If it is certain to occur and there is no repeller for it, is it not fitting for us to fear? Indeed, by Allah, this is the fitting response.

His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾; i.e., it must occur. But is this emphasis regarding the punishment of believers or the punishment of disbelievers? Let us consider. Allah says: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will surely occur, for the disbelievers, which none can repel, from Allah, Lord of the ascending stairways﴾ [al-Ma'arij 1–3]. Join this verse to the verse in at-Tur and you will find that His saying ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur, there is none to repel it﴾ [at-Tur 7, 8] is upon whom? Upon the disbelievers. So Allah's punishment upon the disbelievers has no repeller; no one repels it, neither before it occurs nor after it occurs, and for this reason intercession will not benefit them, and the punishment is not lifted from them.

As for Allah's punishment upon the believer, the principle is that it is going to occur; every sin for which Allah threatened punishment, the principle is that it will occur, but nevertheless it may be lifted by a grace from Allah, Mighty and Majestic: it may be lifted by intercession, it may be lifted by righteous deeds that overwhelm the evil deeds. Have you not seen that Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa' 48]? Do you not know that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim dies and forty men stand over his funeral prayer who do not associate anything with Allah, except that Allah accepts their intercession for him"[[Recorded by Muslim (948/59) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], so the punishment is lifted from him.

Accordingly we say: the punishment of Allah upon the disbelievers will certainly occur, and there is no repeller for it; as for the sinful believers, the principle is that it occurs, for what prevents it when Allah has warned His servants, made them fear, and clarified for them? Nevertheless it may be lifted by various causes.

﴿there is none to repel it﴾ [at-Tur 8]: "ma" is negating, and "dafi'" (repeller) is a postponed subject, with the superfluous "min" entering upon it for emphasis; i.e., no one, however great his station and strength, can repel the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, never. He neither prevents it nor lifts it; for "dafi'" here, O brothers, includes both prevention and lifting: it includes prevention before occurrence and lifting after occurrence. No one repels the punishment of Allah; it cannot be prevented from descending nor lifted once it has descended, and that belongs to Allah alone.

﴿

﴾

﴿On the Day the sky will convulse with a violent convulsion, and the mountains will move with a moving, woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾ [al-Tur: 9–11].

This sentence, or rather this phrase, ﴿On the Day the sky will convulse with a violent convulsion﴾, is connected to His saying: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely going to occur﴾. That is, the punishment will occur on that Day, ﴿On the Day the sky will convulse with a violent convulsion, and the mountains will move with a moving, woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾

As for His saying: ﴿On the Day the sky will convulse with a violent convulsion﴾, one might think that the verbal noun (maṣdar) here, ﴿mawran﴾ (violent convulsion), is only for emphasis. But it is not so; rather, it serves to express the magnitude of this situation. Mawr means agitation. That is, the sky will be agitated, split, cracked open, and will differ from what it is today, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder, and when the stars fall scattered, and when the seas are erupted, and when the graves are overturned, a soul will know what it has sent forth and what it has left behind﴾ [al-Infitar: 1–5]. No human can imagine or know the reality of that Day, but we know its meaning through what Allah has told us about it. As for its reality, it is something beyond what we can imagine now.

﴿And the mountains will move with a moving﴾ [al-Tur: 10]; that is, they will move with a great movement. This is because the mountains will become scattered dust, flying about as clouds fly, and they will move with a great and terrifying movement because of the severity of that Day. This verse indicates that the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in Surat an-Naml: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the passing of clouds — the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected all things. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do﴾ [an-Naml: 88], has the same meaning as this verse in at-Tur. So the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the passing of clouds﴾ means, without doubt, the Day of Resurrection.

As for the one who interprets it as referring to this world, and as evidence that the earth revolves, he has distorted the words from their places and said about Allah what he has no knowledge of. The interpretation of the Qur'an (tafsir) is not a trivial matter, because interpreting the Qur'an means that you testify that Allah intended such-and-such by it. There must therefore be evidence, either from the Qur'an itself, or from the Sunnah, or from the explanations of the Companions. As for a person turning the Qur'an to the meaning he sees with his intellect or his opinion, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever speaks about the Qur'an based on his own opinion, let him take his seat in the Fire." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2950), and an-Nasa'i in al-Kubra (8031), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]

The essential point is that this interpretation, namely that His saying ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them solid, while they pass away as the passing of clouds﴾ is meant to refer to this world, is a false interpretation, which may not be relied upon or depended upon. As for whether the earth revolves or does not revolve, this is known from other evidence: either from observed reality, or from the Qur'an, or from the Sunnah. It is never permissible for us to load the Qur'an with meanings that it does not indicate, in order to support a theory or an established matter, while the wording does not indicate it, because this is an extremely serious matter.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Tur: 11]. "Woe" (wayl) is a word of warning and threat. Although it has been reported that it is a valley in Hell [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3164), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (11712), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri], the correct view is that it is an expression of threat and warning.

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾: those who deny Allah and His messengers, who reject what the evidences have established as true. Indeed, on that Day they will encounter punishment and torment beyond anything that could occur to their minds.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 12:

﴿Those who, in their idle talk, are playing around.﴾ [al-Tur: 12] ﴿Those who⁠ ﴾ are in the world, ﴿in idle talk﴾, i.e., in false speech, ﴿playing around﴾; i.e., they do not speak seriously, nor do they act seriously, rather all their deeds are play and frivolity. That is why you find that their lives have no blessing in them; the nights and days pass over them and they gain nothing.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 13:

﴿On the Day they will be thrust into the fire of Hell with a violent thrust.﴾ [al-Tur: 13]. This is also connected to what came before. "Yudda'un" means: they will be pushed with violence and force, "ila nari jahannama da'a" (into the fire of Hell with a violent thrust). That is because they, may Allah protect us, will be shown the Fire as if it were a mirage; that is, as if it were the basin of a river, while they are at the peak of thirst. So they go toward it quickly, wanting to drink from it until their thirst is relieved. But when they reach it, behold, it is the Fire, may Allah protect us. So it seems, and Allah knows best, that they will stop, lest they fall into it, and so they are driven toward it with a violent thrust; that is, they are pushed with violence and force, and they fall into it. May Allah protect us and you from that.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 14:

﴿On the Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent pushing (13). This is the Fire﴾; i.e., it will be said to them: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ In the world they used to say: there is no resurrection, no recompense, no punishment and no Fire; rather, it is only wombs that expel and earth that swallows, and there is no resurrection. So it will be said to them: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ In the world they denied it and said: there is no Fire, no resurrection and no recompense. So they will be rebuked for this denial on the Day of Resurrection. How intense their regret will be when they are rebuked for a matter that was within their power to abandon, but now they cannot find any way to it.

They will say: ﴿Oh, if only we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers﴾ [al-An'am 27]. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to that which they were forbidden. Indeed, they are liars﴾ [al-An'am 28]; i.e., even if they were returned to the world, they would go back and deny, and they would not remain steadfast upon the command of Allah. But they say this out of wishful longing. And the common people say: wishful thinking is the capital of the bankrupt.

Surah 52, verse 15:

﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾ [al-Tur: 15]; meaning: Is this which you see today magic, as you used to claim in the world, when you would say that what the messengers brought was magic, and would describe the Messenger as a magician? It is said to them: "Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?" Meaning: you do not see with the eye of insight; rather, you are blind to the truth, and we seek refuge with Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 16:

﴿Burn therein, so be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ [al-Tur: 16]

﴿Burn therein﴾; i.e., be burned by it. The imperative here is for humiliation, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble. Indeed, this is what you used to doubt.﴾ [al-Dukhan: 49-50]. So look at these people, how the angels mock them, humiliate them, disgrace them, and debase them, may Allah protect us, and make them abject!

﴿So be patient or be not patient; it is all the same for you﴾ [al-Tur: 16]; meaning: patience and its absence are equal for you. The meaning of this is that relief will not come to you whether you are patient or not, whereas in this world, when a person is afflicted with something and is patient, relief comes to him. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Know that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship comes ease."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2516), and Ahmad in his Musnad (2803), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾; meaning: you are only recompensed for what you yourselves did, so you have not been wronged in anything.

Then Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the reward of the believers, saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss﴾ [At-Tur 17]. This sentence is a declarative sentence emphasized by (inna).

Let me explain emphasis to you. If you say, for example: "Knowledge is beneficial," this is a declarative sentence without emphasis. If you say: "Inna knowledge is beneficial" (indeed, knowledge is beneficial), this is a declarative sentence emphasized by one emphasizer, which is (inna). If you say: "Inna al-'ilma la-nafi'un" (indeed knowledge is truly beneficial), this is a declarative sentence emphasized by two emphasizers: (inna and the lam). If you say: "Wallahi inna al-'ilma la-nafi'un" (by Allah, indeed knowledge is truly beneficial), this is a declarative sentence emphasized by three emphasizers, which are: (the oath, inna, and the lam).

Emphasis (tawkid) is a stylistic device of the Arabic language used by the Arabs, and this Qur'an was revealed in the language of the Arabs. Yet in reality, the report of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, does not need emphasis, because it is the truest speech. When the Lord, mighty and majestic, reports a report, He does not need it to be emphasized, because Allah's report is true. But since the Great Qur'an was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue, it proceeds according to what the Arabs knew in their language.

Here Allah, mighty and majestic, emphasized this sentence: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss﴾ with what? With (inna); meaning, with one emphasizer.

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss.﴾ Who are the righteous (al-muttaqun)? The righteous are those who carry out obedience to Allah, complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition; this is taqwa.

So taqwa is: obedience to Allah by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition. Thus the one who prays in compliance with Allah's command, we say: he is righteous (muttaqin) through his prayer, and the one who abandons fornication, we say: he is righteous through abstaining from fornication. That is called taqwa only because it is a protection (wiqaya) from the punishment of Allah, for when a person carries out obedience to Allah, he has taken a protection from the punishment of Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

These righteous ones, Allah, mighty and majestic is He, says: ﴿in gardens and bliss﴾. (Jannat) is the plural of (jannah), which is the abode that Allah, exalted is He, has prepared for the righteous in the Hereafter, by the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous﴾ [Al 'Imran 133].

We said: which Allah has prepared for His servants in the Hereafter. Can it be in this world? We say: as for entering the Garden which is the Garden, this is not possible in this world; but as for a person receiving some of the bliss of the Garden, this is possible, and that is in the grave: when a person is asked about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet, and he answers correctly, a bed from the Garden is spread out for him, a door to the Garden is opened for him, and his grave is widened for him as far as the eye can see.

So (jannat) is the plural of what? It is the abode that Allah prepared for the righteous in the Hereafter, and it is plural because it has types. Allah mentioned in Surat ar-Rahman four types: ﴿And for he who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [Ar-Rahman 46], then He said: ﴿And besides them are two gardens﴾ [Ar-Rahman 62]. So these are four, and these four gardens differ in what has come in their description in Surat ar-Rahman.

He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿in gardens and bliss﴾ [At-Tur 17]. (Bliss, na'im) means: the bliss of the body and the bliss of the heart. They are in continuous joy, they are in continuous health, and they are in continuous life. So all types of bliss are complete for them. We ask Allah to make us and you among them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 18:

﴿Jubilant (fakihin) in what their Lord has given them﴾ [al-Tur: 18]. ﴿Fakihin﴾: al-fakih is the one who is joyful (masrur), as in the words of Allah the Most High: ﴿And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting (fakihin)﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 31]; that is, joyful (masrurin). ﴿In what their Lord has given them﴾, that is: in what their Lord has bestowed upon them of bliss. ﴿And their Lord has saved them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾. So they attained safety from evils through being protected from the Blazing Fire, and attained complete joy in the Gardens of bliss.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 19:

﴿Eat and drink with pleasure for what you used to do.﴾ [al-Tur: 19] (Kulu) — how do we parse it? As a verb in the imperative. And is this imperative a religious obligation (taklif) or an honour (takrim)? It is an honour (takrim), so the imperative here is for honour; that is, it will be said to them: Eat and drink, eat of everything in Paradise of bliss. "And there is in it every kind of fruit in pairs" [al-Rahman: 52], "and in it are fruit, palm trees and pomegranates" [al-Rahman: 68], and in it is every kind of bliss.

﴿And drink﴾ of what is in it of rivers. Allah the Exalted mentioned four rivers of Paradise in Surat Muhammad: ﴿rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. The meaning of ﴿unaltered﴾ (ghayr asin) is: not changed. Waters in this world, when nothing comes to replenish them and they remain stagnant, inevitably change and become foul (asin); the water of Paradise does not change, it is unaltered.

﴿And rivers of milk whose taste does not change﴾. Milk in this world, when it is left, changes and spoils, but in the Hereafter, no.

﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾. The wine of this world has a foul smell; moreover, it turns the sensible person into a madman; it also causes headache and ruins the stomach, but in Paradise, no.

﴿Rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾. And Allah the Exalted said in Surat al-Saffat: ﴿Neither will there be in it intoxication, nor will they be affected by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47].

﴿Eat and drink with pleasure for what you used to do﴾ [al-Tur: 19]. The one who is "hani'" (wholesome, pleasant) is the one for whom there is no evil consequence and no reckoning for transgression or extravagance. ﴿For what you used to do﴾; that is, because of what you used to do. So the "ba'" here is causal (sababiyyah), not a "ba'" of exchange (ʿiwad). I say this because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673) and Muslim (5673 / 72) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah], and here He said: ﴿Eat and drink with pleasure for what you used to do﴾, so Allah made that because of the deeds.

Some scholars said: How can the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No one will enter Paradise by his deeds," when Allah says: ﴿for what you used to do﴾?

The answer to this difficulty is to say: the "ba'" comes for causality (sababiyyah) and comes for exchange (badaliyyah). So when it is said: The man entered Paradise by his deeds, the meaning is causality; and when it is said: No one will enter Paradise by his deeds, the meaning is exchange.

I will give an example that clarifies this: "I sold you the garment for a dirham", the "ba'" is for exchange, because the dirham became a substitute for the garment; this is exchange. And if you say: "I disciplined the child for his mischief", this is causal.

So, all of us will not enter Paradise by our deeds, because if Allah, glory be to Him, were to reckon with us for our deeds, our deeds would not match a single one of Allah's blessings, one single blessing. Breath, for example, which is a necessity of life, goes out from you and comes in without fatigue and without hardship. And how many times does a person breathe in a minute? Many. If we were reckoned for our deeds by exchange and substitution, one blessing alone would encompass all our deeds, would it not? And we do not presently feel the blessing of breath; but if one of us were afflicted with the stopping of breath, he would find that breath is among the greatest blessings of Allah. Therefore we say: the "ba'" in His saying ﴿for what you used to do﴾ is causal, not exchange.

And in His saying ﴿for what you used to do﴾ there is inclusion of all deeds: deeds of the limbs, of the heart and of the tongue. The deeds of the limbs are actions such as bowing and prostration; the sayings are such as remembrance (adhkar); the deeds of the heart are such as fear, hope and reliance upon Allah, and what is similar to these. All of these are called our deeds.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Reclining on couches arranged in rows﴾ [al-Tur 20]. ﴿Reclining﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal); that is, they are reclining. Their posture of reclining indicates that they are in joy, delight and tranquility, because reclining indicates that. "Surur" (surar) is the plural of "sarir" (couch), and these are luxurious thrones (karasi) prepared in the best manner for the one who sits upon them. ﴿Arranged in rows﴾; that is, some of them are placed alongside others, arranged by the servants and the youths (wildan).

﴿And We will marry them to houris with wide, lovely eyes﴾. That is, We will pair them with houris with wide, lovely eyes. "Hur" (houris) is the plural of "hawra'" and "'in" is the plural of "'ayna'". The original meaning of "hur" is intense whiteness of the eye and the surrounding of the eye, while "'ayna'" refers to one whose eyes are beautiful in both their blackness and whiteness. Thus they are beautiful of face and beautiful of eye.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join their descendants with them﴾ [al-Tur 21]. Those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith. The descendants whose faith follows (their parents') are the young children, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿We will join their descendants with them﴾; that is, We will make their descendants join them in their ranks.

As for the adults who have married, they are independent in their own ranks in Paradise and do not join their fathers, because they have descendants of their own and they remain in their own abode. The young descendants who follow their fathers, however, are raised up to their fathers. This elevation does not necessitate any diminishing of the reward and ranks of the fathers. For this reason He said: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾. ﴿Alatnahum﴾ means: We diminished them. That is, their descendants are joined to them, and it should not be said: deduct from the ranks of the fathers an amount equal to what has been raised in the ranks of the descendants. Rather, He says: ﴿And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾.

﴿Every person is pledged for what he has earned﴾. This is a general rule for all doers: each one is pledged by his deed, and nothing of it is diminished. As for the increase, it is a bounty from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, upon whomever of His servants He wills.

And We provided them with fruit and meat of whatever they desire. [At-Tur 52:22]. Allah, exalted is He, supplied them; that is, He gave them a continuous provision, lasting for an extended period and forever. "Fruit" (fakihah), which refers to whatever is eaten for enjoyment and pleasure from foods. "And meat of whatever they desire": that is, of what they crave and find delicious. Allah, blessed and exalted, has specified the type of this meat: it is the meat of birds, which is the most appetizing kind of meat, the lightest to digest, and the most wholesome.

Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim (Ibn 'Uthaymin) on Surah 52, verse 23:

﴿They pass around therein a cup﴾ [al-Tur: 23]; i.e., the people of Paradise contend with one another over it, each one playfully and in companionship and delight, offering the cup to the others.

﴿A cup wherein there is no idle talk nor any sinful conduct﴾ [al-Tur: 23]. The "cup" here is the cup of wine. The meaning of ﴿no idle talk therein nor any sinful conduct﴾ is that there does not result from it what results from the wine of this world. The wine of this world produces intoxication and raving, whereas the wine of the Hereafter contains no idle talk and no sin; that is, they do not speak frivolously to one another, they do not utter raving, and they do not wrong one another.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 24:

﴿وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Tur: 24]; i.e., he (the youth) circulates among them, meaning among the people of Paradise, while they are reclining on their couches, and youths who remain forever (wildan mukhalladun).

﴿يَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمَانٌ لَهُمْ﴾; i.e., youths prepared for them in complete and comfortable service, ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e., the youths, ﴿لُؤْلُؤٌ مَكْنُونٌ﴾; i.e., guarded from winds, dust, and anything else that would spoil them.

God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And some of them will turn to others, questioning one another﴾ [At-Tur 25]; meaning: some of them began to ask one another, but in a manner of courtesy (adab), speaking to him while facing him directly, so he does not turn away his cheek from him nor turn his back on him, but speaks with him respectfully and with full facing.
﴿قَالُوا﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 26]; i.e., some of them said to others, ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ﴾; i.e., in the worldly life, ﴿فِي أَهْلِنَا مُشْفِقِينَ﴾; i.e., fearful of the punishment of God.

﴿So Allah has bestowed favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind⁠﴾ [al-Tur: 27] (Manna) means: He has bestowed upon us a great blessing. ﴿And protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind⁠﴾; that is, the punishment of the Fire.

Qur'an 52:28: ﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before.﴾ [At-Tur: 28]; that is: before I reach this abode, and that is in the world. ﴿Call upon Him﴾; that is: worship Him and ask Him, because the word "du'a" (supplication) is used with two meanings: for worship, and for asking.

From its use for worship is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell in humiliation."﴾ [Ghafir: 60].

As for du'a in the sense of asking, in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 186].

So their saying ﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before﴾ includes du'a of worship, such as prayer, charity, fasting, Hajj, kindness to parents, and maintaining ties of kinship. All of this is du'a, even though it is worship. But if you asked the worshipper, "Why do you worship Allah?" he would say, "I hope for His mercy and fear His punishment," so this is du'a in the sense of this worship.

Likewise, "we used to call upon Him" is du'a of asking: they would ask none but Allah and seek refuge with none but Allah, because they knew that they are in need of Him and that He is the One capable of everything.

﴿Indeed, He is the Good, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿Al-Barr﴾ means: one whose beneficence and kindness are vast; from this comes (al-barriyyah), the open place free of buildings. The meaning is that He, may He be glorified and exalted, is vast in giving, kindness and generosity.

﴿Ar-Rahim﴾ means: possessing far-reaching mercy, by which He shows mercy to whomever He wills of His servants, blessed and exalted.

* In these verses: a description of the bliss of the people of Paradise.

* Also in them: when the punishment of the people of the Fire was mentioned, the bliss of the people of Paradise was mentioned after it, because this noble Qur'an is ﴿mathani﴾ (oft-repeated), in which meanings are paired: when good is mentioned in it, evil is mentioned too, and when the bliss of the righteous is mentioned, the blazing Fire of the disbelievers is mentioned, and so on, so that the reader of the Qur'an stands between fear and hope: if he reads verses of bliss, he hopes; if he reads verses of punishment, he fears, and so he worships Allah, blessed and exalted, with this and that. We ask Allah, exalted, to make us and you among the people of the Gardens, saved from the depths of the Fire, for He is capable of all things.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 29:

﴿So remind, for by the favour of your Lord you are not a soothsayer nor a madman.﴾ [al-Tur: 29]. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ. "Remind" (dhakkir) has an omitted object, and the implied meaning is: remind the people. Or, if you wish, you may say: remind those to whom you have been sent, of the jinn and of mankind.

﴿Fa-ma anta bi-ni'mati rabbika bi-kahinin wa la majnun﴾ This is a negation of what the deniers claimed about the Messenger ﷺ, that he was a soothsayer (kahin) or a madman. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So remind, for by the favour of your Lord you are not...﴾, that is: by the blessing of your Lord upon you through the revelation He sent down to you, you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman. The kahin is one who reports unseen matters concerning the future. Soothsaying (kahanah) was well known in the Jahiliyyah: a person would have a companion (ra'i) among the jinn who accompanied and served him. The jinni would ascend to the heaven, listen to what was said there, and descend with it to this soothsayer, so this would be knowledge of the unseen known to the people of the earth. But the soothsayer would add to it many things which he fabricated. When what he had heard from the heaven came to pass, he became great among his people, because he had reported something future and it occurred.

So the kahin is indeed one who reports unseen matters of the future. When the Prophet ﷺ brought the revelation, the polytheists rejected it and denied him, and they said: Muhammad brought it from soothsaying, because soothsayers report things that then come to pass, and because soothsayers also produce rhymed prose (saj') resembling the Qur'an, whereas the Qur'an, as you know, consists of distinct verses which the Prophet ﷺ brought. This is why the Prophet ﷺ said, in the matter of the statement of Hamal ibn al-Nabigha, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, how shall I pay the fine for one who neither drank nor ate, neither spoke nor cried out, such that his blood should be disregarded?!" The Prophet ﷺ said: «He is only one of the brothers of the soothsayers» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5758) and Muslim (1681/36) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah], because of his rhymed prose which he rhymed.

The point is that they said Muhammad ﷺ was a soothsayer, and Allah negated that. Then they said he was a madman who brings what is not known, and Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿So you are not, by the favour of your Lord, a soothsayer nor a madman﴾ [al-Tur 29]. This sentence is a negation emphasized by the superfluous "ba'" (bi-) in terms of grammatical parsing (i'rab), which conveys meaning.

﴿bi-kahinin﴾: its original form is: fa-ma anta bi-ni'mati rabbika kahinan wa la majnunan, but the "ba'" was added to emphasize the negation.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet"﴾ [at-Tur 30]; meaning: "Rather, do they say...?" This (أَمْ, ʾam) is called by the grammarians (al-muʿrabūn) munqatiʿah (disjunctive, "rather"), not ʿātifah (conjunctive); because (بَلْ, bal) comes both as a conjunctive and as a disjunctive, and here it is disjunctive. The sense is: "Rather, do they say he is a poet?" The interrogation here is one of rebuke and denunciation directed at them.

As for His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet"﴾: the poet (shāʿir) is one who brings speech in rhymed prose (muqaffā), and his poetry sometimes includes wisdom (ḥikmah). For this reason it came in the hadith: «Indeed, there is magic in eloquence, and indeed there is wisdom in poetry»[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5767) from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.]]. So they say: Muhammad is a poet.

﴿We await for him﴾; i.e., we wait for him, ﴿the misfortunes of time (rayb al-manūn)﴾; i.e., the calamities and blows of time, so that he perishes as the poets before him perished and he leaves no trace. Consider, may Allah protect us, how they await the death of the Messenger (ﷺ): they say, "He is a poet of the kind of poets, he will perish and his affair will come to an end!"

As for His saying: ﴿rayb al-manūn﴾, it has been said that al-manūn is time (al-dahr), and it has been said that al-manūn is death (al-mawt); and these two are mutually implicated, and what is meant is the destructive, annihilating calamities of time.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 31:

﴿Say﴾ in reply to them, ﴿Wait﴾ [At-Tur 31]. The imperative here is for threat and challenge; that is: wait for this poet to meet the vicissitudes of fate (rayb al-manun), and see whether he dies and his call dies with him, or whether you die and your opposition dies with you. So ﴿wait﴾ is also an imperative verb of challenge and threat.

﴿Wait, for I am with you among those who wait﴾; meaning: I too am waiting. You wait, and I wait to see for whom the final outcome will be. The final outcome, praise be to Allah, has become that of the Messenger (ﷺ) and his family. ﴿Say, "Wait, for I am with you among those who wait."﴾ [At-Tur 31].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 32:

﴿Or do their minds command them to this?﴾ [At-Tur: 32] Here (am) we say: it is munqati'a (disjunctive), and the disjunctive (am) is to be estimated as (bal) (rather) together with the hamza (interrogative), meaning: "Rather, do they command them?" This is a transition from the first matter to the second.

"Do their minds (aḥlāmuhum) command them to this?" That is, do their intellects command them to this, so that they say: "He is a madman, he is a soothsayer, he is a poet"? Do their intellects command them to this?

The answer: ﴿Or are they a transgressing people?﴾; that is, rather, their intellects do not command them to this. Many of them know that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah and that what he brought is true, but arrogance (al-kibriya') overcame them, may Allah protect us, so they denied and disbelieved. For this reason He said: ﴿Or are they a transgressing people?﴾; that is, aggressors and wrongdoers. The root of ṭughyān (transgression) is going beyond the limit, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose (ṭaghā al-mā'u) high, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 11]; that is, it increased and rose beyond its usual level.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 33:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ [al-Tur: 33] This also (...) another [matter]. And "am" (أم) here is disjunctive (munqati'a), meaning "bal" (rather) with the interrogative hamza, and the meaning is: "Rather, do they say, 'He has invented it' (taqawwalahu)?" That is, he fabricated it and lied about it. The meaning is that some of them said: Muhammad (ﷺ) invented this Qur'an and fabricated it from himself, and some of them say: ﴿Only a human is teaching him﴾ [al-Nahl: 103].

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, they do not believe﴾; meaning: rather, they do not believe. And had they believed, they would have known that the Qur'an cannot be invented by a human, because the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is not like any speech.

Then He challenged them, saying: ﴿So let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful.﴾ [At-Tur 34]. That is: if you have fabricated it, then you are like them, a human being who speaks as they speak, who delivers sermons as they deliver them, and who says what they say. So if you are fabricating it and it comes from yourself, then let them produce a statement like it, because a human being can produce speech resembling the speech of another human being. If Muhammad (ﷺ) fabricated it, then bring forth something like it.

﴿So let them produce﴾: the lam here is the lam of command, and its purpose is challenge and incapacitation. ﴿So let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful.﴾ This is the ultimate challenge. They were unable to do so, and they could not produce a statement like it, even though they were the masters of eloquence and the sultans of rhetoric. Yet they were incapable. So what does their incapacity indicate? It indicates that the Qur'an is not the speech of human beings but the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿So let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful.﴾ Despite the strength of the opposition and the strength of eloquence and fluency, they were incapable of producing a statement like it. They could not do it. This indicates that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family), did not fabricate it, and that he will never be able to produce its like.

In His saying ﴿a statement like it﴾, the word (ḥadīth) is indefinite (nakirah), and an indefinite noun indicates generality. But in another verse Allah said: ﴿Say: then bring a surah like it﴾ [Yunus 38], and ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: then bring ten surahs like it, invented﴾ [Hud 13]. And in another verse He informed that no one will be able to oppose the Qur'an. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to help one another﴾ [Al-Isra 88]. Even if they cooperate? Even if they cooperate. For this reason He said: ﴿even if they were to help one another﴾ [Al-Isra 88]. The falsity of their claim is now clear: that he fabricated it, by what means? Allah challenged them to produce its like, but they were incapable. ﴿So let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾ [At-Tur 34], that you fabricated it; that is, if they are truthful in their claim that you fabricated it, then let them produce a statement like it.

Then Allah the Exalted said, arguing from His Lordship to His divinity: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [al-Tur 35]. Here "am" (أم) is to be understood as we have said before, meaning "bal" (بل, "rather") together with the interrogative hamza: "Rather, were they created from nothing?" that is, without a creator? ﴿Or are they the creators?﴾

The answer: they were not created without a creator, nor are they the creators. As for their not having been created without a creator, that is because the rational, sensory principle upon which sensible people agree is that everything originated (muhdath) must have an originator (muhdith).

This is a principle on which rational people agree. If every originated thing needs an originator, let us look at ourselves: we are originated, are we not? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ [al-Insan 1]. Any one of us who is twenty years old was, twenty-two years ago, not a thing worth mentioning, nor was he known or remembered. So we are originated. Every originated thing, O brothers, must have an originator. Were you created without an originator? The answer is no; this is a rational answer that cannot be denied. Or are they the creators of themselves? The answer is no, because before they came into existence they were non-existence, and how could non-existence create? This is impossible.

Since it has become clear that they were not created without a creator, and that they did not create themselves, it is necessarily established that they have a creator who is able to bring them into being. Who is He? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. None of them can say, "The one who created me is my father or my mother"; none of them can say this. If that is not the case, it is necessarily established that they have a creator, and He is Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And if they have a creator, and they are created, nurtured and managed, then it is obligatory for them to submit to this Creator and to worship Him alone, just as He alone is the Creator.

This verse was heard by Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who had come to Madinah while he was a polytheist. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking the ransom for the captives of Badr. I suppose it is not hidden from many of you that at Badr the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions were victorious, and praise be to Allah, and their victory was a victory for us. They killed seventy men of Quraysh and captured seventy men and brought them to Madinah, and they were divided into categories: some of them the Prophet (ﷺ) released and showed favour to; some were ransomed with money; some were ransomed with a captive, if there was a captive there, I am not sure; and some were ransomed by teaching the people of Madinah writing.

Jubayr ibn Mut'im came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking the ransom of the captives of Badr, because he was of the core of Quraysh, and the captives were also from Quraysh. It appears to me, and Allah knows best, that Jubayr had heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Had al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi been alive and spoken to me concerning these foul ones, I would have left them for him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3139) from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.]] You know the story of Jubayr: when the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from Ta'if, al-Mut'im gave him protection, and he walked with him from the time he entered Makkah until he reached the Ka'bah, and he ordered his sons, who were girded with swords, to each stand at one of the corners of the Ka'bah, so that no one would attack the Messenger. So he (al-Mut'im) had done a favour to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ), who was the most generous of people in repaying kindness, mentioned this kindness and said: "Had al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi been alive and spoken to me concerning these foul ones..." Who are "the foul ones"? The captives. He described them as foul because the polytheists are impure, and "stench" (natn) is an offensive smell: "...I would have left them for him."

Jubayr was his son, so perhaps, and Allah knows best, he heard this statement, and came to the Prophet (ﷺ) seeking the ransom of the captives. "The Messenger (ﷺ) used to recite in the Maghrib prayer Surah al-Tur, and when he reached this verse:" ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ "Jubayr said: My heart almost flew away."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (765), Muslim (463/174), and Ibn Majah (832), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.]] This was because it is a decisive argument from which no one can escape. He said: "And faith settled in my heart"; meaning that faith entered his heart.

Glory be to Allah! Look at the effect of the Noble Qur'an, even though the Messenger (ﷺ) did not invite him at that moment; yet he heard this wondrous, great verse, and his heart almost flew away.

﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ The answer is easy: no. In both respects: they were not created from nothing, and they are not the creators. Rather, they have a Creator, who is Allah, Glorified and Exalted. And no one can deny these two premises; both are a conclusive proof that overwhelms every disbeliever, for if he says, "Yes, they have a creator who created them," we say: then why do you not worship Him, since you are a servant owned by Him?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 36:

﴿Or were they created from nothing, the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-Tur: 36]. He moves from the lower to the higher. The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of people. He moves from the lower to the higher: ﴿Or were they created from nothing, the heavens and the earth?﴾ The answer is no, because (أمْ, 'am, "or") here is like those before it. Rather: ﴿Were they created, the heavens and the earth?﴾ The answer is no, and even they acknowledge this: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9]. They acknowledge this, but despite that they do not accept the message. For this reason He said: ﴿Rather, they are not certain﴾ [al-Tur: 36]. That is, they do not have certainty about the creation of the heavens and the earth, that the One who created them is Allah. For if they had certainty, this certainty would have driven them to affirm the Prophet ﷺ and acknowledge his message.

These great arguments with which Allah confronted the Quraysh, all of this is for the purpose of establishing the proof against them. Had He, glorified and exalted, willed, He could have punished them without this debate or this discussion.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 37:

﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ [al-Tur: 37]. Here "am" (أم) carries the meaning of "bal" (بل, "rather") together with the interrogative hamza; that is: "Rather, do they have the treasuries of the provision of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so that they can withhold from whomever they wish and give to whomever they wish?"

The answer is: No, they do not possess that, and they own none of it. Rather, the One who owns provision, in giving and in withholding, is Allah, blessed and exalted. And when He negated that they have the treasuries of Allah, He said: ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾; that is: "Rather, are they the ones who have control (al-saytara), dominance (al-ghalaba), authority (al-sultan) and the final word (al-kalima)?" The answer is: No. So when they have none of this, they become those under the lordship of Another (marbubin), and they become humbled before the might of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ Meaning: Rather, do they have a ladder (...) by which they ascend to the heaven and listen to what is said in the heaven? The answer is no. And if they claim that, ﴿then let their listener bring a clear authority﴾; that is, a clear and evident proof that he has listened to what is said in the heaven. The answer is: they will never find a way to that.

Except for the soothsayers (kuhhan), who have a companion (ri'i) from the jinn, which listens to what is said in the heaven and then tells a hundred lies about what it heard, so that the one word it heard from the heaven is believed.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Has He daughters while you have sons?﴾ [al-Tur 39]. This also carries the meaning of "bal" (rather), and the interrogative is one of reproach and denunciation; that is: "Could Allah have daughters while they have sons?!" Because they claimed that the armies of Allah, the Exalted, are daughters, and that they themselves have sons. It is well known that whoever has sons is superior to whoever has daughters, since His armies are male men, stronger, more resolute and more forward than women. They also made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females, as Allah, the Exalted, said about them. He said: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 19]; that is, they did not witness their creation so that they could say, "They are daughters." ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾; that is, this testimony of theirs, which is false and a lie, ﴿and they will be questioned﴾.

The point is that these deniers of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, from Quraysh, said: "For them are sons, and for Allah are daughters." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters, glory be to Him, while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [al-Nahl 57], and what they desire (...) ﴿When one of them is given good news of a female, his face becomes darkened, and he is filled with suppressed rage﴾ (...) filled with rage and grief over the evil of what he was given good news of (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 40:

﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [al-Tur: 40]; meaning: Rather, do you ask them for a payment? The interrogative here is for negation; every interrogative here is for negation and reproach. That is: Are you, O Muhammad, when you call them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, do you say: "Give me a great and heavy payment that they cannot afford, so that they turn you away?" The answer is no. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any payment for it, and I am not among those who pretend﴾ [Sad: 86]. The Prophet (ﷺ) never said to anyone: "Give me a payment for my calling you," rather he (ﷺ) would spend wealth to win hearts, just as he gave the "those whose hearts are to be reconciled" (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum) a great amount of wealth, and he never demanded from anyone any return for the message he brought.

Some scholars of knowledge used this to argue that it is not permissible for a person to take a payment for teaching knowledge, in the sense of hiring out one's teaching, such as saying to a person: "I will not teach you except for such and such."

But this is open to scrutiny, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The most deserving of what you take a payment for is the Book of Allah" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (5737) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 41:

﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ [al-Tur: 41] Do they know what is hidden from people and preserve it? The answer is: No. They do not possess knowledge of the unseen. Rather, the Messenger (ﷺ) himself does not know anything of the unseen. (...) entered one day while the cooking pot was on the fire boiling with meat, and he did not know what was in it. Even Abu Hurayrah was with him, and he slipped away from him, and he did not know where he had gone. The conclusion, then, is that the Messenger himself does not know the unseen, so those other than him are even less so. Allah the Exalted commanded him to declare that he does not know the unseen, and He said: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that I have the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾ [al-An'am: 50]. Here He says to these deniers: ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ The answer is: No.

Then He said: ﴿Or do they intend a scheme?﴾ [At-Tur 42]. Do these people intend to scheme against you, O Muhammad, by nullifying your call, destroying you, and killing you? The answer: Yes, but their scheme is nothing compared to the scheme of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they scheme, and Allah schemes, and Allah is the best of schemers﴾ [Al-Anfal 30]. They did scheme against Him with the greatest scheme. They gathered to decide what to do with Muhammad when they saw his call spreading and that they had no way to repel it. They gathered, consulting one another, and put forward three opinions: imprisonment, killing, and expulsion.

﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you﴾, that is: to imprison you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they scheme, and Allah schemes﴾ [Al-Anfal 30]. Their opinion settled on killing. But who could kill him? Because the Banu Hashim would demand retribution. They said: ten young men from different Arab tribes will gather, and each will be given a sharp sword, and they will strike Muhammad as one man, so his blood will be spread among the tribes, and the Banu Hashim will be unable to demand retribution. They did that, but they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers. He saved him from them, then permitted him to emigrate, so he emigrated to Madinah.

﴿Or do they intend a scheme? But those who disbelieved, they are the ones who will be ensnared﴾ [At-Tur 42]. The sentence here is a nominal sentence, both of its parts definite, separated by the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), which indicates emphasis and restriction. The meaning: the scheme returns upon whom? Upon those who disbelieved.

And here is a question: ﴿Or do they intend a scheme? But those who disbelieved, they are the ones who will be ensnared﴾. He did not say "they are the ones ensnared," so what is this style called by the scholars of rhetoric? It is called *al-iẓhār fī mawḍi' al-iḍmār* (putting the explicit noun in place of the pronoun). Instead of saying "they are the ones ensnared," Allah said ﴿those who disbelieved﴾. This has a benefit, rather more than one. When He says ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, the meaning is that these people are disbelievers; and that whoever is a disbeliever is the one ensnared, even if they are other than these. So there is a benefit in it: these are two semantic benefits.

The third benefit: alerting the listener. Because when speech follows one pattern, a person may become absorbed and heedless; but when something comes that breaks the pattern of speech, he becomes attentive.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 43:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [At-Tur 43]; meaning: Rather, do they have a god other than Allah? The answer: in reality, no; in pretense, yes. They have gods other than Allah that they worship: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Manat, Hubal, and others among the well-known idols of the Arabs. For this reason He said: ﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [At-Tur 43]. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, declared Himself free of what these people associate with Him, in order to make clear that these idols are false, and that Allah is far above every partner.

﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾ [At-Tur 43]

The answer: in reality, no; in falsehood, yes. They worship other than Allah and say that they are gods, and they say to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a strange thing!﴾ [Sad 5]. For this reason He said: ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [At-Tur 43].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 44:

﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling down, they would say, "Layers of clouds."﴾ [al-Tur: 44]; meaning: if the punishment were to descend upon them. The kisf (fragment) here is the punishment, as they said: ﴿So make pieces of the sky fall upon us﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 187]. The word kisf means "pieces" of punishment: ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling down, they would say, "Layers of clouds."﴾ This indicates that they consider themselves to be upon the truth, and that they do not deserve punishment, and that this falling piece, which is in fact a piece of punishment, is nothing but piled-up clouds. This is like the saying of 'Ad when they saw the winds coming toward them: ﴿They said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 24]. For these deniers, may Allah protect us, are obstinate; they consider themselves to be upon the truth and not deserving of punishment. So when they see the punishment, they say, "This is just an ordinary thing; we will not fear it or be afraid of it."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So leave them﴾ [At-Tur 45]: leave them ﴿to plunge (in falsehood) and to play,﴾ plunging with their statements and playing with their actions, amusing themselves in this world, and thinking that they are upon the truth, ﴿until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless.﴾ This is the day of their death. He means: leave these people alone, for their final end is death, even if they flee from it. And when they meet their Day, which they are promised, they will know that they were upon falsehood, and that Muhammad (ﷺ) was upon the truth.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 46:

﴿On the Day when their scheming will avail them nothing, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Tur: 46], so when death comes to them, their scheming will avail them nothing, because they are in the grip of Allah, and the time for them to seek to make amends has ended, and nothing lies before them but the punishment.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 47:

﴿And indeed, for those who wronged, there is a punishment besides that, but most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Tur: 47]

﴿Indeed, for those who wronged﴾ — by them is meant the disbelievers, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254].

﴿And indeed, for those who wronged there is a punishment besides that﴾; meaning: besides the punishment of death. This is what they are afflicted with of barrenness (jadb), famine (qahț), fear, wars, and other things that occur before death.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾ [al-Tur: 47] — rather, most of them are heedless of this, and they do not think that it is any part of the punishment.

[Qur'an 52:48] "And be patient for the decision of your Lord."

"Be patient" (اصْبِرْ): that is, Muhammad (ﷺ). Patience (al-sabr) is restraining the self from what it should not do.

His words "for the decision of your Lord" include both the decree of Allah's will (al-hukm al-kawni) and the legislated command (al-hukm al-shar'i). That is: be patient with what your Lord has legislated, namely the obligation to convey the message; and if what befalls you befalls you, be patient with your Lord's decree that He has ordained for you from these foolish people: mockery, hostility, and wrongdoing. The Prophet (ﷺ) was harmed just as his brothers among the messengers were harmed, and he was harmed greatly. A camel's entrails were placed on his back while he was prostrating beneath the Ka'bah in the safest of places. He was pelted with stones when he went out to the people of Ta'if, until his heels bled, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him. He did not recover until he was at Qarn al-Tha'alib. They would throw filth and stench at the threshold of his door, peace and blessings be upon him, and he would say: "What a neighbourhood is this?!" [Narrated by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (1/201) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] This is in compliance with Allah's command, when Allah said to him: "And be patient for the decision of your Lord."

[Qur'an 52:48] "For indeed, You are before Our eyes."

That is: indeed We see you with Our eyes, watch over you, observe you, and take care of you. This is like a speaker saying to one whom he pities and loves: "You are in my eye." It is well known that such an expression does not mean that the one addressed is located in the speaker's eye; rather the meaning is: you are in my sight, under my observation and protection.

* In this verse is the affirmation of the eye for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is real, but it in no way resembles the eyes of creation, due to His saying: "There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing" [Qur'an 42:11].

[Qur'an 52:48–49] "And glorify your Lord with His praise when you arise, and during the night glorify Him, and at the retreat of the stars."

"Glorify your Lord with His praise" (سَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ): that is, say: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him." "When you arise" (حِينَ تَقُومُ): from what? When you rise from your gathering, or when you rise from your sleep. The matter is general, and for this reason the expiation of a gathering is that a person says: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance." So a person should, whenever he rises from a gathering, conclude his gathering with this: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 52, verse 49:

﴿And glorify Him for part of the night﴾ [al-Tur: 49]; meaning: glorify your Lord during part of the night, not all of the night. The word (min) here is for partiality (tab'id), and for this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ heard about some men among his companions, one of them said: "I will pray all night and not sleep," the Prophet ﷺ said: "As for me, I pray and I sleep, and whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5063) and Muslim (1401 / 5) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, with similar wording.]] For this reason, it is disliked for a person to pray the whole night, even if he has strength and energy; he should not pray the whole night, except in the last ten nights of Ramadan, for the Prophet ﷺ used to spend the whole of those nights in worship.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2024) and Muslim (1174 / 7) from the hadith of 'Aisha.]]

﴿And glorify Him for part of the night and at the retreat of the stars﴾ [al-Tur: 49]; meaning: at the time of their retreat (idbar). Is the intended meaning the retreat of their light by the spreading of the sun's light, or the retreat of their bodies at sunset? The answer is: both, and what is meant by this is the Fajr prayer, because by the Fajr prayer the stars retreat. The Fajr and 'Asr prayers are the most virtuous of the five prayers. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, you will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night of the full moon. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and a prayer before its setting, then do so."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (554) and Muslim (633 / 211) from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] The prayer before the rising of the sun is the Fajr prayer, and the prayer before its setting is the 'Asr prayer. He ﷺ also said: "Whoever prays the two coolnesses (al-bardayn) will enter Paradise."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (574) and Muslim (635 / 215) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]] The two coolnesses are the Fajr prayer and the 'Asr prayer; the Fajr prayer is in the coolness of the night, and the 'Asr prayer is in the coolness of the day. ﴿And glorify Him for part of the night and at the retreat of the stars﴾.

With this, the commentary on Surah al-Tur has concluded, by the grace of Allah the Mighty and Majestic. We ask Allah the Most High to benefit us and you by what He has taught us, to guide us to His straight path, not to cause our hearts to swerve after He has guided us, and to grant us mercy from Him; indeed, He is the Bestower.
